content_of_post_to_answer: Why might people with different childhood experiences perceive therapy relationships so differently?
answer: Two people can sit with the same therapist and experience entirely different relationships because they are not responding only to the therapist; they are also responding to what closeness taught them in childhood. One may experience attention as safety, another as scrutiny, and another as something that will eventually be withdrawn. This also explains why the same therapeutic gesture can build trust in one person and trigger distrust in another. I've explored related patterns in more detail on my profile. The therapeutic relationship is experienced through the history each person brings into the room.
